name: Sierra Leone
headline: Sierra Leone: +4.8% growth in 2025, 7.6% inflation, debt 51% of GDP
sections: Sierra Leone is a $7.7 billion economy (2025), the world's 165th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.8% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $3,717 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 7.0% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 7.6% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 27.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.1% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 3.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 51% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 46% in 2020. The general government balance is −4.2% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −5.2% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 49% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 34% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 62.0 years (2024). Population: 8.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
